inconsistencies: Settings/arguments stack: #31260 claims to be the foundation for runtime checking in #16545, while #16545 is described as the base of #17580, #17493, #17783 and #17581. The true base must be settled before review; otherwise read #16545 -> #17580 -> #17783/#17493 -> #17581 in that order.
util::Result stack: #25665 is the base for #26022, #25722 and #29700; #25722 additionally needs #26022. Review #25665 first, then #26022, then #25722/#29700.
Logging macro chain: #34778 is the base for #29256, which in turn (with #33847) is a base for #30342. #34778 was scored below both; it is promoted here and must be reviewed first.

#34038 and #35387 solve the same problem (making trace/loglevel usable standalone and controllable via RPC) by different designs; reviewer #35387's own thread names #34038 as the competing alternative. Review #34038 first since #35355 and #34730 are stacked on it, then decide #35387.
#35322 and #35355 both replace the log-level map plus mutex with atomic category bitmasks; the two overlap substantially and should not be reviewed independently.
#36190 is a test-only follow-up to the runtime fix in #36105; it has no value until #36105 lands.
#32966 (receiving) and #35302 (sending) are halves of the same BIP352 project; receiving carries the libsecp256k1 primitives and should be reviewed first.
#26966 (thread pool) and #36603 (blocking queue) each introduce general-purpose concurrency utilities for the shared codebase; the two primitives should be reconciled rather than landed separately.
#27409 changes default datadir resolution including symlink redirection, and #36373 logs the symlink-resolved datadir; #27409 should be settled first since it may change what should be logged.
#19460 depends on #10102 and #29409, neither of which appears in this category, so its utils-side value cannot be judged independently here.
result.notes: The category previously had no P1 despite containing three fixes whose failure mode is data loss, process abort, or out-of-bounds memory access; those three are raised so that the P2 band is not asked to cover both 'config option silently ignored' and 'reindex destroys block files'. Much of the list is a small number of long author stacks (settings typing, util::Result, logging macros); ordering within those stacks follows dependency order rather than individual score.
